name: Acute Posterior Multifocal Placoid Pigment Epitheliopathy
aliases: Acute Posterior Multifocal Placoid Pigment Epitheliopathy Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of multiple, flat, cream-colored placoid lesions at the level of the retinal pigment epithelium and choroid
Acute onset of bilateral visual disturbances including scotomas and decreased visual acuity
Characteristic early hypofluorescence and late hyperfluorescence of lesions on fluorescein angiography
Exclusion of infectious or other inflammatory causes mimicking APMPPE

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multifocal placoid lesions with acute bilateral visual symptoms and characteristic fluorescein angiography findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by imaging; exclusion of other posterior uveitis causes is essential

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multifocal placoid lesions of the retinal pigment epithelium
searchTerms: multiple flat white spots on retina
patchy lesions in eye pigment layer
sudden blind spots in both eyes
acute loss of parts of vision
both eyes with dark visual areas

pathognomonic.symptomName: Characteristic fluorescein angiography pattern with early hypofluorescence and late staining
searchTerms: eye imaging showing early dark areas and late bright spots
fluorescein eye test with delayed staining
pain in head prior to vision changes

occasional.symptomName: Mild vitritis (inflammatory cells in vitreous humor)
searchTerms: few inflammatory cells in eye gel

occasional.symptomName: Transient neurological symptoms including mild meningismus
searchTerms: temporary neurological symptoms with neck stiffness
brief nerve symptoms with mild meningitis signs
transient brain symptoms with neck pain
brain blood vessel inflammation causing neurological problems
cerebral vessel inflammation with nerve deficits

rare.symptomName: Persistent visual field defects after resolution

searchTerms: new abnormal blood vessels in eye

laboratory: Normal or mildly elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP)
CSF analysis may show mild pleocytosis if neurological symptoms present
imaging: Fluorescein angiography showing early hypofluorescence and late staining of placoid lesions
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) demonstrating disruption of outer retinal layers
MRI brain may show white matter lesions if neurological involvement
other: Exclusion of infectious etiologies such as syphilis, tuberculosis, and viral infections
Negative serologic tests for autoimmune markers

distinguishingFeatures: Progressive geographic choroidal lesions with recurrent course
Presence of demyelinating lesions on MRI
Multiple cream-colored choroidal lesions with characteristic HLA-A29 association

redFlags: Neurological symptoms suggestive of cerebral vasculitis
references: Jampol LM, Sieving PA, Pugh D, Fishman GA, Gilbert H. Acute posterior multifocal placoid pigment epitheliopathy. I. Clinical findings. Arch Ophthalmol. 1988;106(2): 233-239.
Watzke RC, Packer AJ, Folk JC, et al. Acute posterior multifocal placoid pigment epitheliopathy. Am J Ophthalmol. 1984;98(2): 161-170.
Orphanet: Acute posterior multifocal placoid pigment epitheliopathy (ORPHA:714164)
